findings.text: Native shared memory control entry accepts segment identifier with operation selector and user buffer and delegates to central dispatcher using modern version handling with legacy variant deriving version from selector before delegating same way.

Supported control operation set comprises global limit inquiry and usage summary inquiry and descriptor status inquiries and attribute update and removal and memory lock operations with user memory faults on copy failure and invalid request on unknown selector.

Memory lock management requires either interprocess communication locking capability in caller namespace or ownership match against owner or creator identity with additional memory lock resource limit requirement for lock requests and huge page backed segments bypass state changes while still succeeding.

Locked indicator in permission mode moves from clear to set only on successful backing store lock acquisition with capture of current user count reference and moves from set to clear on unlock request with release of backing mapping and clearing of stored reference with redundant unlock treated as successful without effect.

Control down path holds read side critical section together with object lock during validation and mutation and normally releases object lock before releasing read side section with unlock completion retaining additional file reference across lock releases to safely release backing mapping after locks are dropped.

Legacy compatibility descriptor layout carries permission substructure followed by segment size and old width timestamps for attach and detach and change and creator and last operator compact process identifiers and attach count with padding and compatibility pointer spares.

Compatibility limits structure carries resource values for maximum size and minimum size and maximum count and maximum per process attachments and total pages plus reserved slots all in compatibility wide unsigned form.
Compatibility usage summary carries used identifier count plus totals for resident and swapped pages and attempt and success counters for swap activity using compatibility integer widths.
Compatibility message kludge carries message buffer pointer plus message type in compatibility widths.
Process listing interface descriptor carries path name plus header text plus table selector plus show callback for rendering each entry.
Process listing iteration state carries interprocess communication namespace plus process identifier namespace plus interface descriptor pointer.

Compatibility transfer helpers always clear destination staging before filling and cap reported maximum segment size to signed integer range and select wide time split layout versus legacy layout based on version and accept only permission substructure on input while ignoring remaining fields.

Compatibility control supports same operation set as native path with compatibility conversions for limit and summary and status inquiries and permission only input for update and rejects negative inputs and resolves caller namespace with legacy compatibility entry deriving version before delegating.

Shared memory attach helper maps existing segment into caller address space honoring caller supplied address and flags and alignment boundary returning mapped address through output parameter and status as return value.

Attach address handling enforces alignment against supplied boundary and allows rounding down when requested while rejecting empty result under remap and requires fixed placement when address supplied and forbids remap without address and derives read versus read write protection plus execute extension and corresponding access mode from caller flags.

Attach authorization requires namespace resolution with lookup under read side protection and access evaluation against permission state and security policy approval and validity confirmation under object lock with teardown treated as removed identifier.

Attach synchronizes lookup under read side lock plus object lock and file creation without locks and address space mutation under killable write lock and attach count adjustment under table write semaphore with exclusive segment lock.

Attach count increments while holding stable file reference before mapping and always decrements after mapping attempt triggering segment destruction when teardown condition holds with private attachment state binding identifier plus namespace reference plus base file.

Native and compatibility attach entries forward caller identifier and address and flags to shared attach helper using respective alignment boundary and report mapped address as successful return value.
Detach helper removes shared memory mappings that start at supplied address requiring page alignment and holding address space write lock across search and unmapping.

Under paged memory management detach eligibility requires shared memory operations and offset relation matching displacement from supplied address with continuation bounded by aligned segment extent and same backing file whereas without memory management detached mapping requires exact start equality.

Shared memory status listing reports key and identifier and mode and segment size and creator and last operator process numbers translated into listing namespace and attach count and owner and group and creator identities mapped into viewer namespace and event times and resident and swapped byte totals derived from page counters.
Size field width in status listing depends on native word width using narrower decimal width on narrow builds and wider width otherwise.
Compatibility attach alignment requirement equals native attach alignment requirement in shared memory attach and multiplexed compatibility paths.
System multiplex entries for interprocess communication accept combined operation code plus generic arguments and delegate to central multiplex helpers for native and compatibility execution.

Supported multiplex set spans message creation and legacy control and send and version dependent receive and shared memory creation and legacy control and attach and detach and semaphore creation and legacy control and timed and untimed wait with high portion of operation code carrying version and low portion selecting function and unknown selectors reported as unimplemented.

Compatibility multiplex converts user pointers through compatibility layer and gates timed semaphore wait on legacy time support and validates message queue inputs for negativity and handles legacy message kludge with compatibility widths and truncates shared memory size argument to narrow width and stores attach result through compatibility width destination.
Early initialization creates system interprocess communication directory in process filesystem and initializes semaphore and message and shared memory subsystems before reporting success.
Key hash table parameters anchor hash linkage and key location within permission structure and size the key to key field width and enable automatic shrinking.
Process listing position maps to table index with fixed offset adjustment acquiring read side protection and object lock on successful lookup and releasing previously held object before advancing.
Process iteration holds object lock on currently displayed entry across show callback releasing it before searching for next position.
Process operations table is forward declared for later definition.

Address arithmetic hazards include wraparound on end calculation and overlap with existing mappings during attach and fragment landing beyond segment extent plus width mismatch during detach sweep mitigated by explicit checks and width unified comparisons.

Lifetime hazards involve segment teardown racing attach and control paths and outer file outliving segment during remap emulation addressed by holding base file reference and validating object under lock and matching count increment with decrement and retaining reference across lock release for mapping teardown.

User interaction hazards include faulty user buffers and interruptible lock acquisition and malformed selectors and misaligned addresses and access to removed objects each reported with distinct failure outcome without partial state change except for defined count adjustments.
